scale_meaning.1: Critical / clearly dangerous - must be reviewed immediately
scale_meaning.2: Likely a real attack or vulnerability - worth review
scale_meaning.3: Uncertain / moderate - could go either way
scale_meaning.4: Low severity - probably not worth analyst time
scale_meaning.5: Clearly informational / noise - not a real threat

note: This is a DRAFT rubric. Review/edit before treating it as final - domain judgement (from you / your supervisor) should override these where they disagree.

rules.rationale: Classtype indicates active exploitation or malware command-and-control activity, not passive traffic.

rules.description: Attack-signature language in the alert message
rules.rationale: The alert message itself names a known attack technique.
Reconnaissance is a precursor to an attack but is not itself confirmed compromise.
Policy/compliance-type signatures (e.g. device/User-Agent detection) generally reflect low technical risk.
Signature is descriptive/observational rather than attack-indicating.

rules.description: Targets a sensitive admin/management or database service
rules.rationale: Destination port is a privileged administrative or database service - raises concern by one tier regardless of the base classtype.
A referenced CVE indicates a known, documented vulnerability rather than a generic heuristic match.
